messages:
jess_support: :rotating_light: Customer OrbitLabs reporting repeated 504s and p95 timeouts on hosted inference API since ~09:12 UTC. They see a huge backlog in our request queue and continuous-batching backlog spiking. They repro consistently with a bursty fanout job.
oncall_sre: sending link to telemetry and paging logs, thx. can you paste the request IDs or tenant id?
jess_support: tenant=orbitlabs-prod, sample request ids: req_01G1AA..., req_01G1BB... (customer redacted). They reported queue depth hitting ~5200 and 504s at the gateway. They attached curl repro. Here's the basic repro they shared:

```
curl -i -X POST "https://api.redwood-hosted.com/v1/generate" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-large","input":"<lot-of-parallel-requests>","max_tokens":256}'
```

maya_eng: looking at our internal dashboards now. continuous_batcher_queue_length for pool hosted-prod-gpu-12 spiked at 09:11-09:18 and stayed high. p95 server latency from batcher -> runtime also rose. suspecting continuous batching consolidation window piling up with many long-context requests.
eli_infra: autoscaler logs show a shortfall of free batch slots; pool scaled but lagged. deploy-bot: autoscaler triggered scale-up: +8 pods at 09:15, but nodes started after 60s. Not enough to catch the tail. 
oncall_sre: can we validate queue depth and the gateway early-reject threshold? maybe our request_queue_limit is set to 5000 and we hit the limit -> gateway starts rejecting/504ing.
ops_rohan: confirmed: gateway metrics show request_queue_count for orbitlabs-prod peaked at 5198, request_queue_limit configured at 5000, tail-timeout hits at 30s -> 504s. Also see many requests in batching queue stuck waiting for prefix/kvcache warmup.
maya_eng: quick mitigation: enable tenant throttling (soft reject) and bump queue_limit to 10k for the pool to buy time while we diag. proposing steps in sequence. 
jess_support: customer is on a paid plan and is escalating; they want ETA on fix. please keep them updated.
eli_infra: immediate action: raise gateway.queue_limit for tenant filter to 10000 and enable throttle policy orbitlabs->throttle30. Doing config patch now (will roll 2 nodes at a time).
maya_eng: while patching, check continuous-batching parameters. The batching consolidation window is set to 200ms for this pool which is too high for bursty short requests; reducing to 50ms should reduce queue hold time and tail latency.

--- commands / checks ---

oncall_sre: commands I ran:

```
# queue depth
curl -s "http://metrics-api.internal:9090/api/v1/query?query=request_queue_count{tenant=\"orbitlabs-prod\"}" | jq .
# check batcher backlog
kubectl -n hosted-prod get pods -l app=continuous-batcher -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name} {.status.containerStatuses[0].restartCount}\n{end}'
```

ops_rohan: sample gateway log snippet showing early rejects and timeouts:

```
[09:14:53] [gateway] tenant=orbitlabs-prod req=req_01G1AA... status=queued position=4987
[09:15:23] [gateway] tenant=orbitlabs-prod req=req_01G1AA... status=timeout code=504 elapsed=30s
[09:15:24] [gateway] tenant=orbitlabs-prod reject reason=queue_limit
```

maya_eng: repro steps we used locally (simulates customer):
1) spawn 1200 parallel curl processes hitting /v1/generate with long prompt (2k tokens)
2) keep concurrency steady for ~5 minutes
3) observe queue_count and batcher backlog

I reproduced 504s and saw batcher hold times > 250ms.

eli_infra: mitigation status: increased gateway queue_limit for orbitlabs-prod to 10000 at 09:29 UTC, applied tenant throttle policy (throttle 60rps per token_key) at 09:31 UTC. Also decreased batching.window_ms to 50 for hosted-prod-gpu-12 pool at 09:36. Rolling restart of 4 batcher pods starting now.

deploy-bot: rollout: continuous-batcher config v1.2.3 -> started rolling update (4 pods) at 09:36:02 UTC

maya_eng: after changes, metrics show queue_count back under 800 within 2m. p95 latency dropped from 3.4s to 0.9s. tail timeouts reduced to near zero. Customer reports improved success rate.

jess_support: customer notified of mitigation at 09:45 UTC. They will keep load low until we confirm stability. They asked for a root cause analysis and a durable fix.

oncall_sre: next actions (TODO):
- eng to investigate why batching.window_ms was non-optimal for this pool workload (maya, eli)
- infra to add an alert when queue_count > 4000 for more than 60s per tenant (ops_rohan)
- product to check tenant plan vs rate limits and consider adaptive throttling docs (jess_support)

maya_eng: preliminary RCA: workload pattern (many simultaneous long-context generations) + high batching.window_ms + delayed autoscaler scale-up caused backlog and queue limit triggers. Fixes: lower batching.window_ms, improve autoscaler headroom policy, and implement per-tenant adaptive throttling to avoid hard queue_limit flips.

eli_infra: follow-up: will implement an autoscaler fast-path that pre-warms additional pods when ephemeral queue slope > X/sec. ETA for patch: 2 weeks.

ops_rohan: created follow-up ticket INC-2026 for alerting and tenant policy changes, assigned to eng/infra.

jess_support: customer satisfied with mitigation for now. We'll plan a postmortem and send RCA to OrbitLabs.

maya_eng: linking to logs and dashboards:
- internal dashboard: https://dashboards.internal/redwood/queues?pool=hosted-prod-gpu-12&tenant=orbitlabs-prod
- log query: https://logs.internal/redwood?q=tenant:orbitlabs-prod%20%22queue_limit%22

eli_infra: marking incident as mitigated. Will keep monitoring for 24h and follow up with postmortem.

ops_rohan: :thumbsup: closing thread once postmortem is posted.
